subject: midly 0.5.3: a timecode division word whose high byte is 0x80
lead: reported by the si-jam-sessions ingest agent (agent-measured), then reproduced here under the compile oracle and read in midly's source; the std-unnamed setup (checks 7-11) is the si-jam-sessions law crate's root at 19d8c29 (#![no_std], extern crate alloc, extern crate std as _, no handler, no allocator, panic = "abort" in dev and release), a design reading there, measured here
compiler: rustc 1.98.1, oracle set jam-strict (midly 0.5.3, alloc + strict; the prebuilt rlibs are debug builds, so overflow checks are on inside midly, as the si-jam lock's release profile requires)

source.fact: Timing::read computes `let fps = -(bit_range!(raw, 8..16) as i8);`: a high byte of 0x80 is -128i8, whose negation overflows
parse unwraps a RIFF file to its RMID data chunk (`Some(b"RIFF") => riff::unwrap(raw)?`) before any strict logic, and Chunk::read skips an unknown chunk id (`_ => ()`) in both builds

checks.label: strict parse of division 0x80 0x00 panics: attempt to negate with overflow
checks.stdout: panicked: attempt to negate with overflow

checks.label: 0x80 as i8 has no checked negation; wrapping gives 128
0x81 returns Err and 0xE8 0xE7 0xE3 0xE2 parse; none of them panic
a wasm32 export that parses division 0x80 traps instead of returning a status
strict parse skips an unknown chunk and unwraps an RMID RIFF file

unknown chunk: ok, tracks 1
rmid: ok, tracks 1

checks.label: recipe 4's export with a trapping panic handler traps on division 0x80
dev profile: std linked unnamed, recipe 4's export traps on division 0x80
release profile: std linked unnamed, recipe 4's export traps on division 0x80

conclusion: Smf::parse panics ('attempt to negate with overflow') on a division word starting 0x80 when overflow checks are on, and a wasm32 export that parses it traps. 0x81 returns an Err, and 0xE8/0xE7/0xE3/0xE2 parse as 24/25/29/30 fps. Rejecting Timing::Timecode after parsing cannot catch it: refuse a timecode division word (bit 15 set) before calling midly. Even with strict, midly unwraps RIFF RMID files and skips unknown chunks. A no_std panic handler that loops turns this, or any, panic into a hang; one that calls core::arch::wasm32::unreachable() traps. So does a crate that links std unnamed (`extern crate std as _;`) with panic=abort and no handler of its own.
panic_handler: Wave 5's recipe 4 (export-smpte-refusal-and-error-kind-mapping-from-wasm32-strict-cdylib) is #![no_std] with `#[panic_handler] fn panic(..) -> ! { loop {} }`. Its verifier ran the recipe's own export on division 0x80: it hung (no return within 20 s), not a trap. The same export with the handler body `core::arch::wasm32::unreachable()` traps (check 6), so the host sees a RuntimeError instead of a call that never returns. A crate with no handler of its own that links std unnamed (`extern crate std as _;`, panic=abort) traps too, under dev and release flags, and its module imports nothing; a 96-PPQ control returns 0, so std's allocator works there. A std path in that crate does not resolve (E0433), but one `extern crate std;` line in any module binds the name again and compiles, so the `_` binding is a review boundary.
